Rows 44-46: column 21 B, column 26 w, column 31 B, column 36 w, column 41 w.
So 5 slots: [B, w, B, w, w]. The black ones have black ticks, the gray ones have gray ticks.
Hmm, this looks like a "level selector" or a "progress indicator" — 5 levels, 2 of which are black (completed/active?). Or maybe a "lives" display.
What else is there? The white spout (rows 44-47, columns 32-44): row 44: W at column 50?? Let me recheck: row 44: "BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBWBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB" — W at column 50. Hmm, that's strange — a single W at (44,50). Row 45: W at columns 32-44. Row 46: W at column 32. So the spout: a horizontal bar at row 45 (columns 32-44), a vertical line at column 32 (rows 45-46), and a single pixel at (44,50)? That's odd. Actually, the W at (44,50) might be part of the white panel's border (the panel's border is at column 50, rows 8-43; row 44 extends 1 pixel further). Yes, the panel's right border is at column 50, rows 8-43, and the W at (44,50) is probably the corner extension of the border.
So the spout = a white "L" at rows 45-46, columns 32-44 (a 13-pixel bar + 1 pixel below column 32). Below it, the droplet.
This strongly resembles a faucet dripping water. The checkerboard panel might be a "tank" to be filled? Or the yellow shapes might be "obstacles"?
Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider the whole thing. This might be a game like "Water Sort" or "Pipe Mania"... but with only MOUSE actions and a static board, the interactions are probably: click on a cell of the checkerboard to change its color, and the goal is to make the yellow shapes match something? But clicking on yellow did nothing.
Maybe the click has to be on a non-yellow cell of the checkerboard to toggle it. Let me try clicking on a black cell of the checkerboard, e.g. (10, 14) (the B block at rows 9-12, columns 14-17). If the cell toggles to c or yellow, that's the mechanic.
Or, the game might be: the two yellow shapes are "pieces" that need to be moved to specific positions by clicking? But the click did nothing.
Let me try clicking on the black squares of the strip (42, 21) and (42, 31) — they might be buttons (e.g. "start" / "reset").
Actually, wait — maybe I should think about the 5 slots as "5 sub-levels" and the black ones as "active". The 2 black slots at positions 1 and 3... hmm.
Or, this might be a "Simon" game: the yellow shapes light up in sequence, and you have to click them in order. But the board is static and there's no animation between frames (the timer just shrinks).
Let me try a few probes in one batch: click (42,21) [black slot 1], then diff; click (42,31) [black slot 3], then diff. Actually, it's better to do one probe at a time to attribute the changes. But each probe costs a timer pixel; the timer is long (60 pixels) so it's fine.
